quotes.text: In terms of injuries, and in terms of the squad, we are having the last training session tomorrow, so no one is ruled out for us for Friday. So, I prefer to be cautious and we will wait till tomorrow to take the final decision on every player.
He is getting closer and tomorrow, we will take a final decision in the team and in the squad that is coming to Brentford.
No, it was just a decision for Tuesday and we will see his development. Tomorrow, we will decide.
Amar will be also not able to play on Saturday.
Still not a real update on Anthony. I have just spoken with him now. I think, in the next 30 minutes, he will have an MRI, so we will get more clarity then. We hope that it is not that serious.
It will be a young midfield. I heard just also from a pundit [asking] why I was playing with such young players – because we have only young players in the squad! JJ [Ramsey] is injured as well.
[Other than] Savona and Milenkovic, all other players will be fit.

But on the other side, we also could see that both were a little bit struggling physically at the end. I think this is what we still need to improve, and that there are no doubts that they can play even 100 minutes or 105 minutes if it’s necessary.

Igor Jesus scored a goal now as well. He was rewarded with the Golden Shoe of the Europa League because he can score goals, but he’s, let’s say, more the ‘playing’ striker, dropping into the pocket, and then we had no striker with power and runs in behind. This is what we were looking for and yeah, I think that’s exactly what Liam [Delap] showed.
I think it’s more or less the same as the other night, yeah. So, nothing has really changed on that front.
He’s in the concussion protocol. So, seven days off, and after this, he will go to the national team. Everything is fine. He’s good. This is the most important [thing], now. He will miss this game.
Morita is still out. The plan is that he will join us after the first week of the international break.
We will see. We are very cautious with him and unfortunately, he cannot help the team.
I would expect not available, yeah.

I thought he was fantastic. He’s a very, very good player. He’s 18 years of age but he’s come in with a real maturity on and off the pitch and it was good to see a player of such ability and composure come in and play the way he played. I thought he was great and it’s just a start.
Haji’s on track, but he’s not obviously ready soon.
In form, in the opponent, in the relationship that we have within that unit, there are a lot of factors [in deciding who starts between Eze and Christos Tzolis on the left].
quotes.about: Eberechi Eze on the left wing

quotes.text: Everyone is ready to go. We are in the same place we were, the three long-term injuries plus Federico. The others, nothing. Okay, we still need to train tomorrow and travel, but everyone is fine.
It is really short term [with Luke], to be honest, but it’s just working towards the game. So, we’ll see how he is come the weekend.
Porro, Tonali, Maddison, all are available to play. Normally, we have to understand the situation in terms of physical condition, but all of them are ready.
We have so many players injured. It’s difficult to mention every one. Marco is out, Onana, Cisse out, Pau, Maatsen out, Goretzka out, Madjo out. I think that’s enough. The other players are ready.

I think that the best thing for Femi is that he uses this [international break] to get back on his highest physical level and then get used to our style of play. Then, we will try to work with him individually and hopefully integrate him back into the team, then definitely after the international break, he will be on a top level and we can use him in games.
He’s young, he will recover fast. He definitely will be an option for tomorrow.
We’ll see. We have different options. It’s one of these options.
quotes.about: if Dayann Methalie comes in for Reinildo this weekend

quotes.text: Merlin Röhl is not available yet, hopefully he’ll be ready at the end of the international break.

For now, we hope that three or four players are ready to be in the squad. I think Joe[linton], you saw already [in the open training session last week], he was partially invovled there. He’s now progressing, he’s doing better and better. Also, one of the others is coming back, definitely, and this is helpful, for sure, but we need to be smart as well in the load management. They have the potential to be in the squad but, for sure, not in the starting XI.

They have returned but not everyone was today in. I have allowed some of them an extra day [off]. Tomorrow, we will be fully back. We are, in general, pleased [by the lack of new injuries]. Ewen was a difficult one, with a hamstring. He will be out for a couple of months, but the rest should be okay.
It depends, we are going to see. I am not a doctor. It’s a muscle injury and we do [a scan] in some days again, but we are going to miss him, for sure, for four or five weeks.
quotes.about: the length of Alex Scott’s absence

quotes.text: Brooksy is fully in team training.

We have still [got] injuries but most of the lads are back on the pitch with rehab coaches or in parts of training with the team, so yeah, we can see light at the end of the tunnel. Maybe for the Graz [match on Thursday] or the Sunderland game [next Sunday], we’re going to have one or two players back. Nearly everyone is back on the pitch, just Alex [who is not].

It’s a shame for Ballard because he was in a good place and he will be sidelined for a few weeks. A medium-term injury, so we’ll keep you updated. For Brian, like Habib, they are on the same schedule and will be available soon. [Habib is] really close. He’s in a good place. Almost every session is needed for the full recovery. So, in around one week, he’ll be fully available. It’s going to be short-term [for Brobbey, as well]. It’s really positive, we were a bit worried when we saw the video but Brian, just after the game, wasn’t too worried because he experienced different injuries in the past. This one, he was adamant that it wasn’t too serious – and it’s the case. We won’t take too many risks, but it won’t be too long.

Joe Rodon is on his way back in his rehab, he is doing good progress. He has already had individual sessions on the pitch but it’ll be a bit before he’s back in team training. Daniel James will miss the Arsenal game. He is out with a back injury. Jean-Matteo came back with an ankle strain. Looks way better. He was today the first time with us out on the pitch. We have to wait right now [to see] how his body reacts but it seems like there is a chance he is available. Some good news with Harry Wilson after his muscle injury. He’s back in team training since Tuesday. Again, we also have to wait right now [to see] how his body reacts but there is also chance for him to be available.
Milan is back training with us, so that’s good news. We hope he’ll be alright if he comes through the next few days. Kaine is back training with us, which is good. He’s been out for longer.

Josh isn’t back yet and he’s had a baby recently, which is good news for him, but he’ll still be a few more weeks, potentially. Haji and Woolfy are a little bit longer, as well, but working hard and getting there. Haji won’t be back until November. I don’t want to put pressure on because it’s an awkward injury. Aurele is working away. It’s a 2-3 month injury, so we’re working through that.
He’s ready to go. Finally! You have been asking this question and we have used the time with Moi to be back fit. He’s been training good and he’s okay to go.

Yes, they have been able to train, some of them earlier than others. Marco Palestra, as well. So, we have used the time and that was the plan. We knew that against Brenford, we were in with some players struggling, but now they have trained well and they are ready to go. For the next block of games to the next international games, we have five Premier League games and and hopefully they will be available as long [as possible], but for tomorrow they will be good.
quotes.about: Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer and Reece James

quotes.text: He has trained the last week. He’s felt better. We didn’t want to rush because we had enough time. What the most important thing is for Cole is to be fully fit, that he enjoys his game, that he’s feeling okay. Whenever he’s not, like the Brentford game, we could see that he was struggling. Fom the next part, we have a good feeling with him and that he’s feeling better.
He’s not going to be fit for tomorrow. That’s the bad news about this international break, that he picked an injury on his ankle and he’s going to be out for a few weeks.

With Kai, because he had a muscular injury, so I spoke to Jürgen [Klopp] and immediately they sent the player back, as is normal. Ezri because he’s been carrying some issues as well and we had good communication with the England camp about that. Tzolis has a muscle injury and he’s going to be out I think for a few weeks. He’s not available. Ezri and Kai we will see tomorrow.

We have to manage him because he’s been with a few issues since he’s come back from the World Cup and we know the amount of games that he’s played in the last three years. It was the sensible thing to do, and hopefully tomorrow he’s available and some others as well who are in doubt.

Yeah, they are both available. They did incredibly well to be available for the Brighton game, we decided not to use them at the end, especially in the manner that we had to play the last few minutes, but they are both available. And Ben White is available as well.
He’s good, he’s good. He went to Marbella, two or three days off, played golf, recovered, and is ready for Anfield. He is good.

Alex Isak and Cody Gakpo will not play the game. They are not ready. Unfortunately for us, both got injuries during the international break. Cody has an ankle injury. He has had some before in his career and it is a matter of him dealing with the pain. It was a really bad tackle, I think. He is doing things individually but will not be ready for Sunday. Alex has a thigh injury. It is a small injury, but it is a muscle injury, and the same: whenever he feels ready. They both don’t look long term. We will be analysing day to day but they are not going to arrive on Sunday.
He’s fit. He’s ready to go. He didn’t play with the national team the last game because of protection but he should be fine. Still we need to train tomorrow, but he’s fine, yes.

We will maybe recover Fede Chiesa but he hasn’t played any minutes. He’s recovering from an injury but he has been doing a good job in the international break and has been training with the small group we had.
Ben is further away, with the issue he has got. He won’t be ready.
Patrick came off and it looks like he will be out for probably a number of weeks. Nous came off and took a knock. He’s not quite right yet, so we’ll have to see how he is.
Amad has done a little bit of training, Marcus has done a little bit of training, Kobbie has done a little bit of training.
Carlos is improving, he’s trained a lot and is improving.

No, they are available to play. Micky played four games, 90 minutes, around 90 minutes. JP played just three games, the difference is this. JP, yesterday, [his] wife [gave birth] to twins. The emotional aspect, we have to consider also this one, but both are available to play.
quotes.about: Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke

quotes.text: He is available but he lost three/four days in the beginning of this week and the end of the last week. Like I said many times, James is a special player for us, as a player, for sure, but also as a personality. Also Gallagher, I think he is playing well, especially in the last two games, Liverpool and Villa.
Pedro and Mudryk, both are not available. Pedro, I think not for many games. For Mudryk, maybe something more.

He is working well, tomorrow he comes with us, also Porro [for support]. I want all players tomorrow, tonight and tomorrow, but he is working very well. I think he is an example for everyone, Deki Kulusevski. Forget the player, but the example of how he reacted to the injury, the reaction to being unlucky, the character he showed this time, was an example, a reference for everyone. I don’t know [when he’ll play], it’s not just my responsibility. We are working together with the medical staff. They are working very well with him, they have done special work. We have to analyse week by week.
We have to consider the many games in a row for Robertson, van de Ven, Bentancur, and the trip of Bentancur. The decision of the first XI is just for that.

Nikola Milenkovic… returned from injury and played the friendly, was all good, but in a duel, he has a bone bruise and he will miss the game. It’s very painful and he can’t train. The other one is Igor Jesus. He has a muscle injury in his calf and he will be out for a few weeks, how it looks like. So that was not really what we wanted. And the other one who is questionable is Neco Williams. He returned well and was good, he trained with us yesterday but didn’t feel well. He got a fever in the night, so he was not available today. Let’s see how he recovers.

Antoni and Josh definitely won’t be involved tomorrow. The rest of them have been on the grass, been around training. The one benefit of the last few weeks has been players like Nathan, Sepp, Matty [Jensen] getting back up to speed and getting close to a return. So, overall, when the players go away for that length of time and the amount of games some of them played, I think we’ve come through it pretty well. We’re in a good place for the next chapter.

It’s early for us to say, we have still tomorrow’s training. Obviously, they were not ready for last night. We have to wait and see. I think it’s still very early but the same way I said they are not available for the previous games, I leave the chance open this time, yes.

In this period especially, when we are basically playing every three days – almost less than three days – you need more players. That’s why we changed the team a little bit yesterday. We will need to change again at the weekend, we will need to change again when we face Villarreal in another three days. We need everyone, we will need everyone in one moment or the other. Everyone has to be ready because we will need him probably.
Bazo seems to be much better, we’re happy for that. It didn’t look that way during the match. He’s progressing well in the last few days so hopefully he’s able to join the group on Saturday.

Unfortunately, Anthony’s been out for many weeks so now it’s the process to bring him back slowly but surely in a smart way. Hopefully next week he’s about to train again, at least partially, and then we can reintegrate him step by step.

With Tino we need to be cautious and we don’t rush him. We know about his injury situation and history but we’re optimistic in the next few weeks we can bring him back step by step. With JJ it’s a bit different. He’s making progress. Hopefully next week he can join in partially in training and then we can build it from there.

We need to manage it really carefully. We missed them so much. Joe has had more training compared to Dan and the next steps for both of them is to give them more game time. For Dan it will most likely be too soon to get that starting position already as he’s just trained a couple of times but for Joelinton it could be a bit different.

If a player approached you and said, ‘Boss, I am not feeling good, I am a little bit exhausted,’ this is normal because we have other options. We have [Joe] Gelhardt, who scored the goal, which is perfect when you have a lot of quality in that position. Mo came in and also scored, which is great for the team.
He’s come back sharp, he looks good. He’s still a very valued squad member on and off the pitch.

Josh is not yet – he had a baby girl last week. He’s got a little bit of an issue with his ankle – the calf is fine – so he’s not on the training just yet, we hope so in the next 2-3 weeks to progress. And Woolfenden is a little bit longer than that.

At some point probably we need to give him [Haaland] a rest, some days off. We are thinking about this. And not just with Erling, we have some players who fortunately or unfortunately are playing all the games with us, all the games with their international team, Elliot [Anderson], Enzo [Fernandez], Marc [Guehi], Erling, Ruben [Dias], so at some point we need to give them some rest.

Just try to work with him day-by-day. During the international break and since the red card against United has been quite long, but he’s training well, doing well since we started, very positive, very good. And we’ll see for tomorrow, he’s available but we have so many games that we’ll decide if he’s going to start or not. But no doubt he’s going to give us something.

Morgan Gibbs-White is a doubt. He couldn’t train the entire week with us. It looks like he can join tomorrow’s session. He had an individual session today with our rehab coaches. He suffered a minor muscle injury at Palace. We have to see how he reacts today and how he deals with tomorrow’s session, and then we will take the final decision. But luckily the injury doesn’t seem to be very serious. We have a chance that he’s available.

Jannik and Kev have been on the grass this week and we’ll see what tomorrow brings in terms of how much they can do. They are different types of injuries. This week, we’ve had to navigate through a few issues. Those two are some of those who are making their way back from injury. Overall, we’re in a really good place.

It’s no real reflection on him, why he came out of the starting team. We have got a really good squad and really good options. Mamadou has been outstanding since he’s come in. I think everyone knows that with the accolades and plaudits he’s had about the start to his Premier League season and how he came in during pre-season and lit it up. He’s so dynamic in the way he plays and he’s such an infectious player. That hasn’t changed. Mamadou will play a lot more games and a lot more minutes for us. It’s difficult picking the team and the main message to the group is that it’s going to be a long season. We’ve got games coming where the squad will get really tested. If we want to achieve a really special season, we’re going to need everybody.

Piero is evolving really well. Knowing his character and the way he pushes, I’m sure it’s not going to take long. But he will need probably another week or two. Zubi looks much better and we have another session tomorrow. After that, we will assess whether he’s available for Forest. [Christian Tzolis is] doing really well. Yesterday, he had another MRI scan. He’s progressing really well, another one that hopefully we can have back in a few weeks.
Next week, we have another MRI with him to see how the healing process is at the moment. Every sign so far has been very, very positive.

We are all disappointed, especially for him. He wanted to have a good start after the international break. We don’t set timelines but he will be out for several weeks. It won’t be short. We will see after Christmas, time will tell.

We’ll see on Luke and Kobbie. Ben’s [Sesko] still undergoing a few checks before we give any updates on timelines. We’re just trying to be clear on what that looks like, but when we know more we’ll let you know.

Jarrad [Branthwaite] had a little problem really early in the game, so we’ve been having a look at that in the week a little bit. Mykolenko is doing much better, he’s got a chance for the game and Christian [Norgaard] has still got a wee bit to go, but I think I could use him at different times if required. I don’t know I he’s ready to start the game yet.

We’re so pleased about the goals Thierno is scoring right now. Someone told me he’s missed the most big chances in the Premier League but some forwards would say he’s getting in the right place at the right time. As a manager you just want him to score. I’ve said many times this isn’t a team that is going to get loads of goals so when you get the opportunity you’d like him to be more clinical, to score more be a bit cleaner when he gets the chances.
He gets another day of recovery and we will see how he is tomorrow and then we make a decision.
With Yankuba Minteh and Mats Wieffer we could see quite a quick return. For Kaoru Mitoma, I hope he’s back for the international break, but we have to be more patient.
Progression. Joe will still miss this game on week seven so edging closer, good progress. Won’t be too long until team training but not yet.
We have a small problem with Hugo – his groin. We will check today, but I’m not sure if he will be okay for tomorrow. Everyone else is available.

We did yesterday an MRI and the pictures looked really well. So, his progression and his healing is on a good way, better than we expected. It means not that he is ready for Sunderland or for next week, but we can progress his rehab training now. We can bring him back on the pitch to start and see how he responds, and we are not talking about six to eight weeks anymore. We are quite confident that we get him back maybe a little bit earlier.

I don’t know because we will train after the press conference. That why we have to evaluate [Henderson’s] chance to come back in the team, and it’s the same for the other players. It’s not a way to say it, but for the moment I really don’t know.

We have a session this afternoon. They can be all of them available or not. Yesterday they were all improving, and we’ll see this afternoon. Still a doubt. For sure, Erling is the only one 100% available, and the other three we need to wait for today’s session.
quotes.about: Messrs Nunes, Kovacic, O’Reilly and Haaland

quotes.text: Yeah, it depends a little bit on the gameplan. I think they can play all together, yeah.

Since we started, I sat down with Phil two, three times, especially at the beginning, just to show him… I don’t know if ‘love’ is the right word to use but just to show him how important he is. I said many times that I know Phil from years ago, so I know how good he is. For different reasons, the last few years, it was not good enough. But again, I think when you have more players like Phil available, you are a better team, because at the end, it’s a matter of improving players. If you improve the players, you improve the team. So, for me, I think it’s my duty to try to help Phil to be again one of the best players in England.

Yeah, but it’s not a matter of just about one game. The season is very long, many games. The important thing is that again, when we decide to use Phil or to use another player, the important thing is that they are ready. Again, I think for the players, also it’s important that they are happy and they enjoy football.

I always said the same. I think football, at the end, is a team sport. So, it’s not about one player. They are all special, and not one of them is special. So, in the moment that I think you just consider one player special, I think from my point of view, it’s the wrong thing. So for me, Rayan is a top player, but we have another 20 top players. So, they are all different, but at the end it’s a matter of trying to find the right balance between what do we want to do when we have the ball and what do we want to do when we don’t have the ball. I think Rayan, in this moment, is one of the best players in Europe when he’s in the right position. That means when we are able to find him between the lines, it’s always dangerous.

Jannik just had a bit of a troubled week going into the Liverpool game, really. A bit of a knock from international duty crept up on him during the Villa game, and then he wasn’t particularly well for a few days, so it was just a very disruptive week. But he’s been back training the last few days, so he’s back to himself, more or less.

There’s nothing major to note; we’re pretty much as we were last weekend. Some players have taken the next step of their journey back with really good weeks of training. Nathan [Collins], in particular, and Mathias Jensen made another really good step with training, considering that he’s only been back a week or two.

He’s progressing. The ankle has been an annoyance, really, for all of us because Josh’s calf injury has cleared up and now the ankle’s a bit of a problem, so it’s affecting his rehab and his recovery. He’s still not with us out on the grass yet. I know he’ll be frustrated with that. We look forward to him being back outside with us.
